text: We evaluated adaptive label smoothing weighted by per-sample loss drop, with smoothing_max of 0.3, in a weak-to-strong setup using gpt2-medium as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student, across num_seeds of 4. The weak supervisor reached an accuracy of 0.55 and the strong model's ceiling accuracy was 0.86, while the strong student trained on weak labels attained a transfer accuracy of 0.75 with a standard error of 0.03. This corresponds to a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.64 with a standard error of 0.09, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.15. The margin between the method's PGR and the baseline exceeds twice the reported standard error, so the direction of the effect favours the method. However, with only 4 seeds the uncertainty estimate itself is coarse, no standard error is reported for the baseline, and the finding rests on a single weak-strong model pair, so broader generality remains untested.
